newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins firmer after long U.S. rate fall.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins firmer after long U.S. rate fall.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds firmed on Thursday as the market stabilised after a long fall on the 25 basis-point U.S. interest rate hike, and dealers said trading was limp ahead of the U.S. Good Friday holiday.
Dealers said nationwide Russian protests unpaid wages and pensions failed to have an impact on the market, as protestor turnout was very far the 20 million forecast by trade union organisers.

"Protests were not massive, so there was no influence," Sberbank dealer Pavel Sool said. "Prices have firmed for the first time after the fall on U.S. rate hike, as the market realised there is still time until May".
Recent U.S. statistics data brought many market analysts to believe that yet another U.S. short-term interest rate rise could come in May.
MinFins closely track Brady Bonds and other emerging market debt.
"Nothing real happened today with MinFins as tomorrow is Good Friday and today is a short day," another dealer said.
